item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Five staff were fired as a result of this incompetence, all of whom died shortly after.

This could be worded more elegantly, and more ominously. Since they die right after, you can just say that five staff were slated for removal but were subsequently killed upon [entity].

Overall pretty decent. There are several interesting threads here, such as the strange entity, the rival, and the man who buys but then disappears. However, I will note that since none of the threads are followed up upon, and the threads aren't interesting enough to me to carry the whole thing, no-vote.

item.title: open the door get on the floor
item.content:encoded:
Taste has been described as rich, slightly sweet, and also slightly bloody; travel to Wyoming is not advised if egg is consumed.

That sentence is so foreboding I love it.

The fact that Marshall, Carter & Dark are selling literal freaking dinosaur eggs and some rich fuck out there is making them into very, very, expensive omelettes amuses me to the point where I can safely say this gets my upvote.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Five staff were fired as a result of this incompetence, all of which died shortly after.

"Fired" as a slang term in this sense doesn't turn up in writing for nearly a decade as an Americanism, and would probably be too colloquial for this document. "Discharged" might be better. Also, "all of which" should be "all of whom". Quite nice, otherwise.

item.title: We Only Sell the Finest Author Commentary at Marshall, Carter and Dork.
item.content:encoded:
I'd like to give a special thanks to everyone in chat who helped me with a formatting glitch I kept getting; hopefully that's now resolved.

This was a bit of a pain. I had to convert 2016 currency into 1880s currency, and even then, I'm only 60% sure I got the exchange rate right. But I think it was worth it.

And before I get questions about it: the OLPP is something that was made up for the sole purposes of this document. Basically, since Prometheus Labs wasn't around in the 1800s, I needed an analogue for them.

Anyway, hope you enjoy, and good luck to all the other contestants.
